trade.reads_as: The country each place sits in, as the Atlas of Economic Complexity records its goods trade: what the whole country exports and imports, by sector, in current US dollars. Exports over imports is a trade balance written as a ratio, NOT the share of consumption met by local production: a country that exports cars and imports food can sit at 1.00 and feed nobody. Re-exports are inside the figures (a gateway country like the Netherlands most of all). A country's figure says nothing about its cities; it is the bracket a place's own trade sits inside.
trade.source: Atlas of Economic Complexity, Growth Lab at Harvard University: International Trade Data (HS 92), doi:10.7910/DVN/T4CHWJ, version 18 (2026-04-22), tables hs92_country_year, hs92_country_product_year_1 and _2; Classifications doi:10.7910/DVN/3BAL1O
trade.licence: CC0 1.0 (the Dataverse record); goods trade only, services are a separate Atlas table

food.reads_as: The country each place sits in, as FAO's Food Balance Sheets record its food: for each commodity group, production against production plus imports minus exports, FAO's own self-sufficiency ratio. Above 1 the country grows more than it keeps; below 1 it eats what others grow. The summary weights each group's ratio, capped at 1, by the group's share of the diet's calories, and says how much of the diet the covered groups are. A country figure, never a city's: it is the bracket a place's own food system sits inside.
food.source: FAO, FAOSTAT Food Balance Sheets (2010-), bulk file https://bulks-faostat.fao.org/production/FoodBalanceSheets_E_All_Data.zip (FoodBalanceSheets_E_All_Data_NOFLAG.csv), elements 5511, 5611, 5911 and 664, years [2010, 2023]; country codes from the Atlas classification (M49)

goods.reads_as: The country each place sits in, as the OECD's trade in value added tables read it: of the value added in what the country's households, government and investors buy, the share that was created inside the country, by the industry that created it. 0.38 for manufacturing means 38% of the manufacturing value added embodied in what the country buys was made at home. Value added, not products or tonnes: a car assembled at home from imported parts counts only for the assembly. A country figure, never a city's: it is the bracket a place's own economy sits inside.

energy.reads_as: The country each place sits in, as the World Bank reads its energy: of the energy the country uses, the share it produces itself, which is one minus its net energy imports as a share of use. Above 1 the country produces more than it uses and exports the rest. Net imports are imports less exports, so a country that imports oil and exports gas can read as self-supplied; gross imports are not published here. A country figure, never a city's.
energy.source: World Bank WDI API v2, EG.IMP.CONS.ZS (net energy imports, % of energy use) and EG.USE.PCAP.KG.OE (energy use, kg of oil equivalent per person), 2015-2024, database last updated 2026-10-08

materials.reads_as: The country each place sits in, as the OECD's material flow accounts read it: of the materials the country consumes, in tonnes, the share it extracted inside its own borders. Above 1 the country extracts more than it keeps and exports the rest. Tonnes weigh sand and copper alike; the four groups in the place's JSON tell them apart. The material footprint beside it counts the raw materials embodied in what the country consumes wherever they were dug. A country figure, never a city's.
materials.source: OECD, Material resources: economy-wide material flow accounts, DSD_MATERIAL_RESOURCES@DF_MATERIAL_RESOURCES, measures DEU, IMP, EXP, DMC, MF in tonnes, groups TOT, BIO, MET, IND, FUEL, 2019-2025: https://sdmx.oecd.org/public/rest/data/OECD.ENV.EPI,DSD_MATERIAL_RESOURCES@DF_MATERIAL_RESOURCES,1.0/

water.reads_as: The country each place sits in, as FAO's AQUASTAT reads its water: of the renewable water the country has in a year, the share that originates inside its own borders (one minus the dependency ratio, the share flowing in from other countries). Beside it, the share of what it has that it withdraws. Water is not bought abroad like goods; this says whose rain it lives on. Resources are long-term averages repeated each year. A country figure, never a city's.
water.source: FAO AQUASTAT dissemination system, BigQuery endpoint with the published query (variables 4192, 4157, 4182, 4188, 4263, years 2018-2022): https://api.data.apps.fao.org/api/v2/bigquery

region_bracket.reads_as: For every tracker place: whether a national figure may be split down to it, and why. Refused for a seaport or a national capital (the check says how wrong that would be), not possible without a NUTS2 code, allowed otherwise. The modelled rows are the NUTS2 region that holds the place, not the place: Schwaben for Augsburg, Bretagne for Brest. They are modelled, never measured, and carry the error bar the check measured for a region that makes things.
region_bracket.not_modelled: refused: a port's customs trade lands for the whole country (the check: Hamburg 3-5x under)
